questions.question:

options.text: Situation in which you can start again
An innocent man who has nothing to spend
Provide a clear record to one’s superiors
A person with no crimes to his record

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Situation in which you can start again**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given idiom, '**start off with a clean slate**', means to begin again afresh without considering the past mistakes or failures.

 
 
• **Example**: After the mishap in his last venture, he decided to start off with **a clean slate**.
 
 
 
• The most appropriate meaning of this idiom is given in option 1 - '**Situation in which you can start again**'.
 
 
• **Example**: He moved to a new city with no past connections, giving him the chance to start again with a clean slate.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is- “**Option 1**".

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png]

• Option 3, 'Provide a clear record to one’s superiors'.
 
• Option 4, 'A person with no crimes to his record'.

questions.solution:

• The term **"Judas kiss" **originates from the biblical story where Judas Iscariot betrays Jesus by identifying him to the authorities with a kiss.
 
• It refers to an act appearing as a gesture of friendship or affection, but that is actually motivated by treachery or deceit.
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase suggests that the matrimonial alliance between the two kingdoms is actually a deceitful act masquerading as a friendly act.
 
 
• **For Example - **The promising trade agreement was, in reality, a Judas kiss, disguising the empire's intention to control the resources of the weaker nation.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**.

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

My friend has been a teacher **__since 10 years__**.
questions.solution:
Here, the correct answer is "for 10 years."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The error in the sentence **"My friend has been a teacher since 10 years"** lies in the use of the preposition **"since"** with the duration of time.
 
• This change ensures that the correct preposition is used to indicate the duration of time.
 
• Using **"since"** in this context would imply a specific point in time when your friend became a teacher, which may not be the intended meaning.
 
 
• **Example**: *I have been working at the company for five years **since**__ I graduated from college.*
 
 
 
• Instead, **"for"** is used to indicate the duration of time your friend has been a teacher.
 __
 
• **Example**: *She has been studying French **for**__ six months to prepare for her upcoming trip to Paris.*
 
 
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

 

Correct sentence:* My friend has been a teacher__** for 10 years**__.*
